title: Soft launch traffic probe and KPI checks
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic, checklist-driven plan for executing a staged "quiet" (soft) launch that focuses on traffic shaping and KPI probes rather than a full feature ramp. Intended for product ops + platform + SRE coordination when we need to validate performance, cost, and user experience under controlled conditions before a larger rollout.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: single-region soft launch of feature flagged API route + telemetry instrumentation only. No marketing.
- Primary goals (what we must validate):
  1) Latency SLOs hold at target Q95/Q99 for the chosen cohort sizes.
  2) Cost per 1k tokens remains within forecast band for observed token mix.
  3) No regression in core production flows (auth, routing, billing).
  4) Observability and alerting fire correctly for all failure modes.
  5) Key UX metrics (time-to-first-byte, streamed-first-token) meet acceptance.

Quick timeline (2 week probe window):
- Day -7: Finalize telemetry and metric dashboards, run synthetic baseline.
- Day -3: Canary build deployed to canary fleet; smoke tests green.
- Day 0: Enable feature flag for cohort A (0.5% of traffic) + traffic shaping.
- Day 1-3: Monitor, collect metric deltas, run guided load tests during off-peak hours.
- Day 4-7: Expand cohort to 2% if no regressions; run cost sensitivity test.
- Day 8-14: Decision window — either continue to incremental expansion or rollback and triage.

Cohort and traffic shaping plan:
- Cohorts: A (0.5%), B (2%), C (10% - experimental only).
- Routing policy: sticky by account id hashing to ensure stable KV cache behavior.
- Burst cap: capped at 20rps per account during probe, global cap 2x baseline.
- Traffic injection: use synthetic scripts to inject edge-case tokens and long context sequences representative of target customers.

KPI baseline and acceptance bands (examples):
- Latency (Q95): baseline 140ms, acceptable deviation +30% (<=182ms).
- Latency (Q99): baseline 420ms, acceptable deviation +40% (<=588ms).
- Error rate (5xx): baseline 0.12%, hard stop if >=0.5% sustained over 15m.
- Token cost per 1k (inference only): baseline $1.10, probe threshold +25% for short experiments.
- Availability (per-route): baseline 99.95%, soft-threshold 99.9% for probe.
- UX metric - time-to-first-byte (streaming): baseline 80ms, acceptance <=160ms.

Phase checklist (pre-launch, launch, probe, decision):
- Pre-launch checklist:
  - [ ] Dashboards created: per-route latency, token mix, cost per token, KV cache hit-rate.
  - [ ] A/B feature flags configured with deterministic hashing.
  - [ ] Traffic shaping rules uploaded to edge gateway and verified in staging.
  - [ ] Canary fleet configured with half the autoscale headroom to surface scaling bugs.
  - [ ] Runbooks updated with new alert thresholds and paging matrix.
  - [ ] Customer-impact list prepared for accounts in cohort; support briefed.

- Launch / Probe checklist (operational playbook):
  - [ ] Start with cohort A at 0.5% during off-peak.
  - [ ] Run targeted synthetic tests (long-context, many-tool-calls) for 30m every 3h.
  - [ ] Monitor KPIs on short cadence (5m rollups) for first 6h, 15m rollups after stability.
  - [ ] If error rate crosses hard stop, hit rollback flag and run immediate postmortem.
  - [ ] For cost probe, enable detailed cost-logging to trace per-request model variant and quantization path.

Decision criteria and actions:
- Continue expansion to next cohort if:
  - Q95 and Q99 within acceptance bands for 24h, AND
  - Error rate < 0.2% and no systemic SRE alerts firing, AND
  - Cost variance < probe threshold for two consecutive measurement windows.
- Halt and triage if:
  - Any hard stop breach (error >=0.5% sustained 15m), OR
  - Regressions in downstream services (auth, billing), OR
  - Observability gaps discovered that prevent confident decision-making.

Monitoring and alerting (what to watch):
- Immediate watch list (pages): 5xx spike, sustained Q99 increase >40%, autoscale failures, elevated queue length in request buffers.
- Diagnostic traces: sample 1% of requests from cohort for full trace capture.
- Metrics to push to on-call dashboard: per-model tail latency, cache hit ratio, token distribution by length, model-variant routing counts, cost-per-request.

Contingency playbook (fast rollback steps):
1) Flip feature flag to route 100% traffic to baseline route.
2) Scale up baseline capacity if needed to absorb shed traffic.
3) Page on-call SRE + eng lead and create high-priority incident.
4) Start immediate data capture: recent logs, last 1h traces, autoscaler events.
5) Communicate externally to support and any affected pilot customers.

Post-probe analysis template (what to capture):
- Executive summary: one-line outcome and recommendation (expand / iterate / rollback).
- KPI deltas vs baseline with charts (latency, errors, cost).
- Notable incidents and actions taken.
- Root cause hypothesis for any regressions.
- Action items and owners for next steps.

Open questions and unknowns (notes-to-self style):
- How representative is our synthetic token mix vs real pilot customers? Need sampling from production corpora.
- Should we enable prefix caching for cohort A? Might mask cold-start problems.
- Cost attribution for multi-model routing still requires tagging work in the billing pipeline.

Appendix: quick run commands and quick-links
- Synthetic traffic script: github.com/redwood-inference/traffic-tools/tree/main/soft-probe (run: ./run_probe.sh --cohort A --duration 30m)
- Dashboard: Confluence -> Product Ops -> Soft Launch Probe (CONFLUENCE-1302)
- Incident template: CONFLUENCE-INC/TEMPLATE-LAUNCH

Owner and coordination:
- Primary owner: Asha Kapoor (product-ops) - overall decision authority for probe.
- Engineering lead: Diego Martín (platform infra) - responsible for routing, autoscale, and rollback.
- SRE on-call: Ravi Patel - paging for any hard-stop alerts.
- Support liaison: Claire Huang - triage and customer comms.

Notes for reviewers:
This is intentionally lightweight and operational-first: the idea is to get an early signal on cost and tail latency without full feature exposure. Reviewers: check the KPI bands, the cohort sizing, and the rollback procedure. If we want a longer probe (30d), we need a stronger cost-guard and periodic manual checkpoints.
